name: Turso
tagline: Hosted libSQL databases with replicas, branching, and edge access

pricing.native: Rows read, storage, and database limits
pricing.notes: The pricing model is not safely comparable as one fixed monthly USD amount. Review the official source before publication.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 100 databases; 5 GB storage; 500 million rows read/month; 10 million rows written/month; 3 GB sync/month; 1-day PITR

tiers.name: Developer
tiers.limits: Unlimited databases; 500 active databases/month; 9 GB storage; 2.5 billion reads; 25 million writes; 10 GB sync; 10-day PITR
tiers.notes: Extra active databases cost $0.10 each; usage overages can be enabled.

tiers.name: Scaler
tiers.limits: Unlimited databases; 2,500 active databases/month; 24 GB storage; 100 billion reads; 100 million writes; 24 GB sync; 30-day PITR

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited databases; 10,000 active databases/month; 50 GB storage; 250 billion reads; 250 million writes; 100 GB sync; 90-day PITR
tiers.notes: Extra active databases cost $0.025 each; includes SSO, BYOK and compliance features.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom unlimited-usage, dedicated-cloud or BYOC deployment with 24×7 support

pricing.freeTierCaps: 100 databases; 5 GB storage; 500 million rows read/month; 10 million rows written/month; 3 GB embedded sync/month; 1-day point-in-time restore
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual prices are about 16.7% lower
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid plans can incur per-unit overages for active databases, storage, rows read, rows written and embedded sync; overages must be enabled, otherwise the applicable usage dimension is blocked at its cap

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Turso's durable value is infrastructure, uptime, operations, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a single-server deployment panel for one user that accepts a repository, builds a container, deploys it, shows logs, and supports rollback.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whyPeopleStillPay: Turso: Managed hosting sells a failure domain, on-call team, network, backups, and capacity planning, not merely a deploy button.
ongoingBurden: Own patching, secrets, TLS, backups, monitoring, capacity, incidents, abuse, networking, and data recovery.

priorArt.name: Coolify
priorArt.desc: Self-hosted application deployment and infrastructure control plane.

priorArt.name: Dokku
priorArt.desc: Open-source platform-as-a-service toolkit for a single server.

alternatives.name: Turso Free
alternatives.desc: The same hosted service is unusually generous: 100 databases, replicas, branches, 5 GB, and one-day point-in-time restore.

notes: Credibility row: Turso survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Turso; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Go 1.24 + Docker + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a single-server deployment panel for one user that accepts a repository, builds a container, deploys it, shows logs, and supports rollback.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: multi-region failover; DDoS protection and compliance; 24-hour operations and support.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
